newsitem.title: JAPAN: Omron to invest $2 mln in Harmonix.
newsitem.headline: Omron to invest $2 mln in Harmonix.

text.p: Omron Corp said on Wednesday it would invest $2 million to buy a 19.9 percent stake in Harmonix Corp, a U.S. technological research and development company.
Omron said the deal included the exclusive right to make and sell products using Harmonix-developed wave technology.
Omron will complete the acquisition within a couple of months, an Omron spokesman said.
The wave technology can be used in a wide range of applications, such as high-capacity wireless telecommunications.

The technology is currently restricted to experiments in Japan, but is being used in Europe and the U.S. for telecommunications and automobile radar systems. The Japanese government is expected to ease is restrictions in the future, the spokesman said.
The technology offers 10 times the bandwidth of the standard microwave frequencies and is capable of data-intensive wireless communications.
